title: Camus and the Absurd
welcome_lead: HL French requires two literary works. Camus's L'Etranger and Le Mythe de Sisyphe centre the absurd.
meta_desc: French HL Literature: Camus, L'Etranger and the absurd.
final_note: Meursault watches the sun — and Camus asks why.

concepts.def: The absurd — Camus's name for the clash of human meaning-seeking with a silent universe.
1942 essay by Camus introducing the absurd.
Existentialism — broader movement Camus sits beside.

walkthroughs.body_html: Aujourd'hui, maman est morte. Ou peut-etre hier, je ne sais pas. The flatness of tone announces Meursault's emotional remove.
Meursault kills the Arab on the beach, citing the sun. The scene literalises the absurd: cause without meaning.
Meursault is condemned less for the murder than for not crying at his mother's funeral. Camus indicts social conformity.
